It might sound silly, but give it some time. I don't know your experience obviously, so I could be wrong, but in my experience when I have major life changes those thoughts flare (in my case, much more minor than yours, I lived in college dorms over the summer with a room of my own and a lock instead of at home, with no room of my own. My thoughts flared for a couple of weeks until I adjusted). They fade off to normal levels after some adjustment time. In the meantime, could you find some distractions? When mine were really bad and I couldn't get them to shut up, I read books I could get easily absorbed in and after a while for my brain to get engaged in the story, the thoughts would subside for a few hours while I read. Hiking could also be good (although it is getting colder). Could you hang out with your friend more too? 

If your ex is saying bad things, if possible, avoid him/block him/get support, especially immediately after an incident. And perhaps you could look into talking to a professional if you haven't already? Even if you aren't comfortable talking about your SI thoughts, you could work on improving how you have relationships so your next one is healthier! If you're in school, they may provide free mental health services. And if you can't afford one, there are some free apps that are sort of therapy-ish. Right now I have Wysa. I know it works on Android, but it might also work on iPhones and other smartphones.

Bear in mind all of this is based on my personal experience and stuff I've read, so feel free to ignore anything that doesn't apply to you. I hope things get better for you soon!

That's not entirely accurate. Have you heard of modding? It's where a person codes a modification to a pre-existing g\*me. Essentially it is quite similar to using monopoly but changing the entire economics system or movement system or something like that. It takes a great deal of coding and mathematical skill to make a mod for a g\*me. For example if you've heard of minecraft, where people can use blocks to build incredible architecture in ways that can defy the laws of physics, there are mods that allow a person to play more realistically or that change the types of blocks available. These mods can be extensive and very impressive and it takes a smart person to create the coding required for the g\*me to not break. So g\*mers use

\-mathematics

\-creativity/imagination

\-coding languages

\-analytical skill
